subject: Logic
title: The Trolley Problem
description: A quick, practical guide to The Trolley Problem.

hook.text: A runaway trolley will kill five people. You can pull a lever to divert it—but it will kill one person instead.

buildup.text: Philippa Foot introduced this in 1967 to test whether moral rules are absolute or depend on outcomes.

discovery.text: Utilitarians say pull the lever—five saved beats one lost. Deontologists say actively killing one is always wrong.

twist.text: Now imagine pushing a large man off a bridge to stop the trolley. Same math—but almost everyone refuses.

climax.text: The shift reveals that proximity, physicality, and intention change our moral intuitions even when the math doesn't.

punchline.text: Same outcome, different action, different answer.

quiz.question: What does the trolley problem test?
options: Whether moral judgments depend on rules, outcomes, or both
